role: Overnight stats card (8 boxes: recording length, sleep, deep sleep, HR range, nadir HR+time, peak HRV+time), overnight HR chart with analysis-window band and clock axis, tags & notes block, peak rolling-RMSSD scan, rolling-window HR nadir, and sleep-stat fallbacks (HealthKit total -> HealthKit boundaries -> recording estimate) for the recovery PDF.
types: OvernightReportRenderer: extension — overnight section drawing and stats
OvernightReportRenderer.OvernightStatValues: struct — the 7 values the two stat rows display
OvernightReportRenderer.OvernightSleepStats: struct — sleep/deep minutes, formatted strings and labels for row 1
OvernightReportRenderer.PeakRMSSDResult: struct — peak rolling RMSSD and its ms offset from the first beat
OvernightReportRenderer.PeakScanWindow: struct — scan window size/step (beats) and optional ms time band
toplevel: File-scope private helpers (formatRecordingDuration, overnightHRSamples, overnightHRY, drawOvernightHRGrid, overnightHRPath, strokeTagPill, storedHRStats, nadirOffset, rollingWindowHRStats, rollingHRSamples, rollingHRWindow, inScanBand) plus four nested value types with synthesized memberwise inits; no globals or persistent state.

flags.text: Peak-HRV clock time is anchored on session.startDate while the nadir fallback uses session.rrSeries?.startDate ?? session.startDate and the chart's time axis uses series.startDate; if a session's startDate differs from its RR series start, the 'Peak HRV @ Time' box disagrees with the chart axis by that difference.

PDF overnight clock times and durations come from cumulative RR time (t_ms) added to a start date and never use the series' wall-clock timestamps; the in-app Overnight card formats the same nadir/peak via series.wallClockTime(forTMs:), which uses wallClockMs. After a strap disconnect gap the PDF's 'Nadir @ Time', 'Peak HRV @ Time' and time-axis labels read earlier than the app's, and 'Recording' duration excludes the gap.

Finds the peak rolling RMSSD: scans windows centred in the 30-70% time band; if nothing qualifies (peak 0), rescans the whole recording. Returns the peak value and the peak beat's ms offset from startTimeMs (offset of index 0 when none found).

flags.text: If no window anywhere has >=30 clean beats with RMSSD in (0,300), the report prints 'Peak HRV 0 ms' at the first beat's clock time instead of a missing value.

The PDF searches for peak HRV in 30-70% of the recording span, while the in-app Overnight card searches 30-70% of the HealthKit sleep envelope when sleep boundaries exist, and the help text says the search is over 'your actual sleep — not your recording time'. With a recording that starts well before sleep the PDF's 'Peak HRV' value and time can differ from the app's for the same night.
